Cc: procurement@fresco.com
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent checkout 503s — evidence & remedy request

Hi Jonas,

We observed a spike of 503s on Fresco checkout between 2026-10-06T08:57:00Z and 2026-10-06T09:12:00Z. During that 15-minute window ~12% of checkout attempts failed (we sampled ~7k requests). This caused a noticeable drop in conversions for that morning rush.

Can you confirm whether this period meets Redwood's SLA eligibility for a proportional remedy/credit, and what evidence you need from our side to validate the impact? We'd like:
- confirmation of the outage window you see from the platform side,
- an indication of whether this will be considered a service outage for compensation, and
- a timeline for an RCA/postmortem and any mitigation steps.

I've attached one of the storefront error dumps and a short sample of request ids we captured. Please let us know a single point of contact on Redwood for log handoff and whether you need additional access.

[Attachment: fresco_error_sample.txt (text/plain)]

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Operations
Fresco Commerce
elena@fresco.com

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Intermittent checkout 503s — evidence & remedy request

Elena — thanks for the heads up and the sample file. I've looped in Laura (AE) and Karthik (SRE) to validate the window and start the telemetry pull.

High-level next steps from our side:
- Karthik will run an initial impact verification against our API gateway logs and the routing layer to confirm the 08:57–09:12Z window.
- We'll collect tokenized traces/req IDs you provide and match them to the downstream response codes.
- We'll confirm whether the event meets the SLA definition for an "unavailable" interval vs. transient errors that fall under normal variance.
- After verification we'll propose a remedy path (proportional credit vs. fixed-month credit) — we'll include math and sample calculations.

Can you confirm you can hand over a CSV of request_ids and the storefront timestamps (UTC)? If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute handoff call tomorrow morning to share the trace ingestion steps.

Also attaching a quick capture of the ticket and the initial request for our records.

[Attachment: initial_request.eml]

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Account Manager — Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference

Adding a short SRE summary and what we need to validate the window quickly.

Preliminary notes:
- We see a faint spike in 503 return codes in us-west-2 edge logs that aligns with the 08:58–09:10Z timeframe; magnitude looks lower on our aggregated metrics (~6–8% of requests) but your sampled storefront traffic suggests it was heavier on specific paths.
- To correlate and make a credit decision we need: request_id list (ideally a CSV with request_id, storefront_ts_utc, path), and any client-side error codes you captured.
- We'll pull internal API gateway raw traces and kv-cache hit/miss ratios for the window; this usually yields definitive attribution (routing, backend saturation, or transient auth failures).

Operational timeline:
- T+0–6h: initial log and trace pull (we'll produce a Protobuf log bundle and a short summary).
- T+24h: preliminary impact note + recommendation on remedy (proportional/flat).
- T+72h: full RCA draft.

If Fresco is comfortable sharing the CSV, we can ingest the IDs and return a matched sample (anonymized) that shows the end-to-end flow for affected requests. If we need direct access to your trace store or request headers to decode an ID, we'll seek a scoped access token (read-only).

Attachment: trace_request_template.tsv (headers and expected columns) — please populate and return.

— Karthik Iyer
Senior SRE
Redwood Inference
